intro: Prompt engineering is one turn. Context engineering is the whole conversation: what goes in the window, what stays out, in what order, with which cache breakpoints, with which compaction triggers. It is the highest-leverage skill in agent work today.

items.title: The seven slots of an agent's context window
items.mechanism: (1) system prompt, (2) tool definitions, (3) static instructions / playbook, (4) conversation history, (5) retrieved chunks, (6) scratchpad / thinking, (7) reserved output budget. Each has different growth rate, cacheability, and compaction strategy.
items.tradeoff: Knowing which slot owns what lets you target compaction to the slot that's actually bloating. Without the mental model, agents 'forget things' and 'cost too much' as one undifferentiated problem.

items.title: Order matters: primacy + recency
items.mechanism: Models attend more strongly to the beginning and end of context. Stable, load-bearing instructions go at the very top. Time-sensitive material (current turn's task) goes at the end.
items.tradeoff: Free behavior — costs nothing to apply, has measurable effect. Worst case: critical instructions buried in the middle get ignored.

items.title: Compaction strategies
items.whenToUse: When approaching budget or after N turns.
items.mechanism: (a) Summarize older tool results into a one-paragraph rollup. (b) Sliding window — drop turns past N. (c) Structural — keep IDs and references, drop verbose bodies. (d) LLM-pass compaction — a cheap model rewrites history to a fraction.
items.tradeoff: Saves tokens. Loses fidelity. Best blends: keep recent N turns raw, summarize older.

items.title: Cache breakpoints (Anthropic)
items.whenToUse: Whenever the same system / tool defs / early messages repeat across calls.
items.mechanism: Anthropic prompt caching gives 90% discount on cached input tokens. Place cache_control: { type: 'ephemeral' } at the end of: system prompt, tool definitions, the older portion of conversation. Last turn is never cached.
items.tradeoff: For agents the savings are enormous — system + tools are huge and re-sent every step. Cache hit requires byte-identical prefix; invalidate on system/tool/edit.

items.title: Retrieval vs injection
items.mechanism: Small, stable, always-needed content → inject (system prompt). Large, dynamic, sometimes-needed → retrieve at runtime. Mistakes go both ways: injecting too much bloats; retrieving too late costs latency.
items.tradeoff: Inject everything = cheap retrieval but unbounded context. Retrieve everything = small context but extra hop + relevance bugs.

items.title: Tool result discipline
items.mechanism: Truncate at the tool boundary with an explicit '[truncated: N more chars]' marker. Strip irrelevant fields server-side. Offer paginate-via-tool if the model wants more.
items.tradeoff: Bounds growth without surprising the model. The marker is critical — silent truncation is worse than visible.

pitfalls.title: No per-turn budget
pitfalls.body: Context grows unbounded until the API rejects. Set a target (e.g. 60% of window for input) and compact when crossed.

pitfalls.title: Unbounded thinking blocks
pitfalls.body: Extended thinking is great until it eats half the window. Cap the budget; compact older thinking into 'I previously decided X' summaries.

pitfalls.title: Cache invalidated unexpectedly
pitfalls.body: A 'small' edit to the system prompt invalidates the cache for every running session. Treat cache prefixes as immutable; version them.

pitfalls.title: Duplicate context injection
pitfalls.body: Same retrieved chunk appears 3× across turns because retrieval ran 3×. Dedupe before injection; track what's already in context.

pitfalls.title: No per-turn token telemetry
pitfalls.body: If you don't track tokens-per-turn over time, you cannot see context bloat coming. Log input tokens with a slot breakdown.
